# 2 Baruch Chapter 27 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 2 Baruch Chapter 27 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 27:3 — "slayings of great ones / killing of leaders"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-slayings of-the-great-ones" | Literal: Syriac rabe = great ones, not specifically leaders |
| LOGOS | "the slaying of great ones" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "the killing of leaders" | Interprets "great ones" as political leaders |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "slayings of great ones" (EMET/LOGOS). The Syriac rabe can mean great/mighty ones of any kind — political interpretation is possible but not exclusive.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 27:6 — "withholding of rain / drought"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "[the] withholding-of-rain" | Literal: Syriac uses a "withholding" verb construction |
| LOGOS | "the withholding of rain" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "drought" | Functional equivalent, more concise |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained LOGOS "the withholding of rain." In 2 Baruch's theology, rain is withheld by divine action — not merely a natural phenomenon. The more literal rendering preserves this theological note.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Theological precision.

---

## 27:9 — "the falling of fire and the descent of Sheol"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-falling-of-fire and-[the] descent-of-Sheol" | Literal noun constructs |
| LOGOS | "the falling of fire and the descent of Sheol" | Formal equivalent |
| PNEUMA | "fire falls from above and Sheol opens from below" | Adds directional imagery for drama |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted PNEUMA's rendering for this verse — "fire falls from above and Sheol opens from below" captures the cosmic drama of the text and the above/below opposition that is implied by the pairing. The Syriac imagery supports this directionality.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of PNEUMA. Vivid directional imagery.

---

## 27:13 — "confusion of the mingling / total chaos"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "confusion-of-the-mingling-of-all-the-previous-[parts]-with-the-others" | Hyphenated literal compound |
| LOGOS | "confusion — the mingling of all the foregoing parts with one another" | Formal with explanatory dash |
| PNEUMA | "total chaos — all the horrors of the previous periods mixed together at once" | Dynamic expansion |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "confusion — the mingling of all the foregoing parts with one another." Retains the Syriac structure while being readable. PNEUMA's "total chaos" loses the structural specificity of the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
